classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the ground segment as the hypotenuse, calculate both broken sections using different ratios, and interpret original height as their sum.

content.prompt: A tree snapped into two sections $AB$ and $BC$ in high winds and then fell. The section $BA$ is inclined at $51^{\circ}38'$ to the horizontal and $AC$ is 9.4 metres long. Find the height of the original tree, in metres correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle ABC with horizontal hypotenuse AC, vertex B above it, an interior angle at A and a right-angle square at B. Ordinary geometry and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: AC = 9.4 m; angle BAC = 51 degrees 38 minutes; angle ABC = 90 degrees. Coordinates derive from the given angle and right-angle relationship.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; neither section length nor the original height appears.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\cos 51^{\circ}38' &= \frac{AB}{9.4}\\AB &= 9.4\cos 51^{\circ}38'\\\sin 51^{\circ}38' &= \frac{BC}{9.4}\\BC &= 9.4\sin 51^{\circ}38'\end{align*}$$
The original height is the sum of the two sections.
$$\begin{align*}AB+BC &= 9.4\cos 51^{\circ}38'+9.4\sin 51^{\circ}38'\\&\approx 13.2\ \mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$
